root_cause.text: The aqc111_suspend() callback invokes PM-aware write command functions that internally call usb_autopm_get_interface(), which attempts to resume the device while it is already in the RPM_SUSPENDING state, causing a deadlock in rpm_resume() waiting for a status change that will never occur.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff shows three function calls being changed from PM-aware variants (aqc111_write_cmd, aqc111_write32_cmd) to their _nopm counterparts (aqc111_write_cmd_nopm, aqc111_write32_cmd_nopm) within the aqc111_suspend() callback. The CVE description explicitly traces the deadlock: rpm_suspend() → usb_suspend_both() (sets RPM_SUSPENDING) → aqc111_suspend() → aqc111_write32_cmd() → usb_autopm_get_interface() → pm_runtime_resume_and_get() → rpm_resume() attempting to resume while already suspending, causing the hang.

bic_trace_step.reason: The aqc111_suspend() function contains the vulnerable construct. At line 1260, it calls usbnet_suspend(intf, message) which puts the device into RPM_SUSPENDING state. Subsequently, the function makes multiple calls to PM-aware write command functions: aqc111_write16_cmd_nopm() at lines 1268, 1273, 1278, etc., and critically at lines 1299-1300 it calls aqc111_write_cmd(dev, AQ_WOL_CFG, ...) and aqc111_write32_cmd(dev, AQ_PHY_OPS, ...) which are NOT the _nopm variants.
